newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Indian foreign minister to visit Sri Lanka soon.
newsitem.headline: Indian foreign minister to visit Sri Lanka soon.

text.p: Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral will visit Sri Lanka this month, just as Colombo steps up a campaign to curb separatist Tamil Tiger rebels' activities, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Sunday.
"The Indian foreign minister will visit Sri Lanka late this month for talks with Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar," spokesman Ravinatha Aryasinha told Reuters.

It will be the second meeting of the two foreign ministers in less than a month. Kadirgamar briefed Gujral in a meeting in New York on September 26 on the Sri Lankan forces' recent offensive against the rebels, he said.
They also discussed in New York, where they were attending the United Nations General Assembly, the issue of Tamil refugees fleeing war-ravaged Sri Lanka for southern India.
"The purpose of Mr Gujral's visit is the Joint Commission, but the two ministers could discuss any issues," Aryasinha said.
The joint commission, led by the two ministers, is held regularly by the two countries to promote economic, technical and cultural cooperation.

Colombo describes as terrorists the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), which is fighting for a separate state for minority Tamils in the predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka, and wants the international community to help curb its activites.
Sri Lanka needs neighbouring India's support to block arms supplies and other assistance to the LTTE by the Tamil-dominated southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
"I think Sri Lanka will seek help from India as it is critical for any diplomatic initiative against the LTTE," said an Asian diplomat.

With 50 million Tamil-speaking people, Tamil Nadu has provided a sanctuary for both Tamil residents and rebels since the ethinic war started in 1983. Some 200,000 refugees landed in Tamil Nadu in the 1980s. Many are still in camps there.
But Indian sympathy soured after the 1991 murder of former Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi by a suspected LTTE female suicide bomber during an election campaign in the state.

Sri Lankan forces late last month captured the rebels' northern stronghold of Kilinochchi after eight days of fighting, during which the rebels said 436 Tamil refugees fled to Rameswaram at the southern tip of the Indian subcontinent.
Sri Lankan officials said 2,500 Tamil refugees had made the narrow crossing between Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu since the influx began in July, when the army first launched its offensive on Kilinochchi.
"On refugeees, there is total understanding between the governments of India and Sri Lanka, that Sri Lanka is taking proper steps," Aryashinha said.
Sri Lankan has intensified naval patrols to stop illegal entry into India. Colombo officials say the LTTE has forced the exodus of Tamils.
"The Indian government is well aware of this and from the actions taken and statements coming from Tamil Nadu, it is clear that the matter is under control at this point of time," Aryashinha said.
He said Kadirgamar met foreign ministers of 20 nations in New York and discussed Sri Lanka's 13-year ethnic conflict, in which Sri Lanka says more than 50,000 people have died.
